tactics.title: Code review
tactics.summary: Reads the change the way a reviewer does: what it is for, what it touches, and where its logic, conventions or security fall short.
tactics.when: On every pull request, after the automated checks pass, so reviewers spend attention on what the checks cannot see.

tactics.title: Finding validation
tactics.summary: Checks the findings themselves before anyone acts on them: is there proof, can it happen, is it new, how bad is it, is it in scope.
tactics.when: Whenever a reviewer, human or model, produces more findings than people will read, or findings that are often wrong.

tactics.title: Intent and spec conformance
tactics.summary: Compares the change to what was asked for: the ticket, the plan or spec, the design, the review comments it was meant to address.
tactics.when: When a change implements a ticket, a plan or a design, and before merging, to confirm the thing built is the thing requested.

tactics.title: Threat modeling
tactics.summary: Maps where a system can be attacked, finds the weaknesses behind each entry point and checks which are mitigated and exposed.
tactics.when: On a whole repository periodically, and on changes that add an entry point, a trust boundary or a new dependency on external input.

tactics.title: Feedback and evaluation
tactics.summary: Closes the loop: production errors and missed bugs become new checks, and the reviewers themselves are measured and tuned.
tactics.when: Continuously, once checks and reviewers are in place. Every escaped bug is a missing technique somewhere to the left.

techniques.name: Formatting
techniques.description: A formatter rewrites code to one layout so diffs show only real changes; in CI it runs in check mode and fails on drift.

subtechniques.name: Code formatter
subtechniques.description: One opinionated formatter per language, run on save and in CI.

subtechniques.name: Import ordering
subtechniques.description: Sort and group imports so they never cause conflicts or noise.

subtechniques.name: Check mode gate
subtechniques.description: Run the formatter with --check or --diff in CI so unformatted code fails instead of being rewritten.

Run it once over the whole tree in a single commit and add that commit to .git-blame-ignore-revs.
Add a pre-commit hook that rewrites, and a CI step in check mode that fails.
reverse: Formatter config in pyproject.toml, .prettierrc, rustfmt.toml or biome.json.
A CI step running the formatter with --check, --diff or format --check.
A .git-blame-ignore-revs file pointing at a mass-format commit.

subtechniques.name: Large file guard

Validate CI and app config against published JSON schemas with check-jsonschema.
Run pre-commit run --all-files in CI so the hooks are not optional.

A CI job that runs pre-commit run --all-files.

techniques.description: Proves call sites and data shapes agree across modules: wrong types, unhandled null or None, signatures broken by a change.

Turn on strict flags for new and frequently changed modules first.

reverse: [tool.mypy] or pyrightconfig.json, tsconfig.json with strict flags.
A tsc --noEmit, mypy or pyright step in CI or a typecheck script.

techniques.name: Static application security testing
techniques.description: Finds injection, unsafe APIs, weak crypto and tainted data reaching a sink without running the code.

subtechniques.name: Pattern rules
subtechniques.description: Syntax-aware patterns for dangerous calls and configurations (shell=True, yaml.load, disabled TLS verification).

subtechniques.name: Taint tracking

subtechniques.name: Language security linters

subtechniques.name: Custom rule packs
subtechniques.description: Rules for the framework and helpers your code uses, with tests for each rule.

Write custom rules for your own wrappers (your query builder, your HTTP client), each with a positive and negative test file.

reverse: A codeql-analysis workflow, .semgrep.yml or a rules/ directory with YAML rules.

techniques.name: Secret scanning
techniques.description: Finds credentials and tokens in the working tree and in history before they are pushed or published.

reverse: .gitleaks.toml, .secrets.baseline or a trufflehog step in CI.

techniques.name: Documentation build
techniques.description: Builds documentation as a check so broken cross-references, links and markup fail like code.

subtechniques.name: Link checking
subtechniques.description: Check internal and external links on a schedule.

subtechniques.name: Doctests

techniques.name: Duplicate code detection
techniques.description: Finds copied blocks so a fix in one copy is not missed in the others, and flags new code that re-implements an existing helper.

subtechniques.name: Token clone detection
subtechniques.description: Report token-identical or near-identical blocks above a size threshold.

subtechniques.name: Semantic reuse check

techniques.name: Complexity limits
techniques.description: Measures cyclomatic complexity, function length and nesting and fails when a change pushes a function past a limit.

subtechniques.name: Complexity thresholds
subtechniques.description: Per-function limits on cyclomatic or cognitive complexity.

subtechniques.name: Size budgets
subtechniques.description: Limits on function, file and parameter counts.

techniques.name: API compatibility checking
techniques.description: Diffs a public interface between the base and the change and reports breaking changes: removed endpoints, changed types, narrowed inputs.

techniques.name: Data and control flow analysis
techniques.description: Builds a code property graph or interprocedural model to answer reachability questions: can this null reach that dereference, which callers reach this function.

techniques.name: Dependency audit

subtechniques.name: License policy
subtechniques.description: Allow or deny dependencies by license.

reverse: deny.toml, osv-scanner.toml, a dependency-review workflow or an audit script.

techniques.name: Lockfile consistency

techniques.name: SBOM and provenance

subtechniques.name: SBOM generation

subtechniques.name: Signing and attestation
subtechniques.description: Sign artifacts and attach build provenance (SLSA).

techniques.name: Dependency risk assessment
techniques.description: Judges a new dependency beyond known CVEs: maintenance, project security practices and signs of a malicious package.

subtechniques.name: Project health scoring
subtechniques.description: Score a dependency's repository practices (branch protection, signed releases, CI).

subtechniques.name: Malicious package heuristics

techniques.name: Unit and integration tests
techniques.description: Example-based tests that run the code and assert on behaviour, from single functions up to services with real dependencies.

subtechniques.name: Integration tests with real services

Promote any rule that a pattern can match into a lint rule.
Leave the rest to a reviewer prompt that quotes the rule it applies.
reverse: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules or CONTRIBUTING.md with coding rules.

techniques.name: Reviewers learned from past reviews
techniques.description: Mines a repository's review discussions for recurring feedback and turns each cluster into a reusable review instruction.

subtechniques.name: Discussion mining
subtechniques.description: Collect resolved review threads with the code they were on.

subtechniques.name: Topic clustering
subtechniques.description: Cluster comments into themes with a minimum number of supporting discussions.

subtechniques.name: Instruction distillation
subtechniques.description: Write one instruction per theme with examples from the threads.

subtechniques.name: Memory of facts and rules
subtechniques.description: Extract facts from new discussions and match them to existing rules to update or add them.

craft: Export review threads with their file paths and diffs.
Embed and cluster comments; keep clusters with enough independent threads.
Distill each cluster into an instruction and evaluate it on held-out PRs.
reverse: The instructions on this site are this technique applied to each source repository.

techniques.name: Security-focused review
techniques.description: A reviewer that reads for exploitable behaviour across files: authorization gaps, injection through helpers, unsafe trust between services.

subtechniques.name: Should-review gate
subtechniques.description: Decide from the diff whether a deeper security pass is warranted.

subtechniques.name: Call-chain investigation
subtechniques.description: Follow user input from entry point to sink with a model, file by file.

subtechniques.name: OWASP classification
subtechniques.description: Tag each finding with an OWASP Top 10 category for routing and reporting.

craft: Gate on diff signals: new routes, auth code, deserialization, subprocess, SQL.
Investigate from the entry point to the sink, not file by file.
Require a concrete input that reaches the sink.
reverse: SECURITY.md, threat model docs, or a security review workflow on paths like auth/ or api/.

techniques.name: LLM application security review
techniques.description: Reviews code that calls models for the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications: prompt injection, output handling, excessive agency, unbounded consumption.

subtechniques.name: Static review of LLM call sites
subtechniques.description: Check how untrusted text reaches prompts and how outputs reach tools or HTML.

subtechniques.name: Red-team probing
subtechniques.description: Send adversarial prompts to a running application and score the responses.

subtechniques.name: Runtime input and output scanning
subtechniques.description: Scan prompts and responses in production for injection and leakage.

craft: List every place untrusted text enters a prompt and every place model output is executed or rendered.
Run a red-team suite against those paths in CI.
Cap tokens, tool calls and spend per request.
reverse: promptfoo or garak config, prompt templates, and tool definitions in the repository.

techniques.name: Review question checklists
techniques.description: A fixed bank of questions a reviewer must answer for a kind of change, ranked so the most relevant ones are asked first.

subtechniques.name: Universal questions
subtechniques.description: Questions that apply to any change: error handling, tests, naming.

subtechniques.name: Behavioural questions
subtechniques.description: Questions about what changes for users and callers.

subtechniques.name: Security requirement checklists
subtechniques.description: Verification requirements per area from a standard such as OWASP ASVS.

craft: Start from a published checklist and keep only questions your reviews actually raise.
Tag each question with the kinds of change it applies to.
Rank by relevance to the diff and ask the top few.
reverse: PR templates with checkbox lists, or review guidelines in CONTRIBUTING.md.

techniques.name: Reviewer routing
techniques.description: Chooses which specialist reviewers, human or automated, apply to a change based on its files, topics and history.

subtechniques.name: Path ownership
subtechniques.description: Route by file path ownership rules.

subtechniques.name: Semantic matching
subtechniques.description: Match the change to reviewer descriptions by embedding similarity and reranking.

subtechniques.name: Reviewer merging
subtechniques.description: Combine overlapping reviewers so one concern is not reviewed twice.

craft: Start with CODEOWNERS for humans.
Describe each automated reviewer in one paragraph and match changes to it.
Log which reviewer produced accepted findings and prune the rest.
reverse: CODEOWNERS, review assignment bots, or reviewer config files.

techniques.name: Evidence-backed verification
techniques.description: Re-checks each finding against the code before it is shown: look for counterevidence, require proof, and refute or suppress what does not hold.

subtechniques.name: Counterevidence search
subtechniques.description: Look for guards, callers or tests that show the claimed failure cannot happen.

subtechniques.name: Proof requirement
subtechniques.description: Drop findings that cite no line, input or behaviour.

subtechniques.name: Run to confirm
subtechniques.description: Write and run a test or script that demonstrates the failure.

subtechniques.name: Atomic findings
subtechniques.description: Split findings that make more than one claim so each is verified separately.

craft: Run a second, independent pass per finding with the code and the claim only.
Record a verdict per finding: confirmed, refuted, suppressed or incomplete, with the reason.
Only post confirmed findings; measure refutation rate per reviewer.
reverse: Bot comments that cite evidence, or review tooling that records dismissed findings.

techniques.name: Path reachability check
techniques.description: Decides whether the triggering state can reach the flagged line on this code path, given guards, early returns and types.

subtechniques.name: Guard analysis
subtechniques.description: Find early returns, enclosing conditions and defaults that exclude the trigger.

subtechniques.name: Caller analysis
subtechniques.description: Find a real caller, config or workflow that produces the triggering state.

craft: For each finding, list the callers of the flagged function.
Check each caller for guards that exclude the trigger.
Mark findings with no established producer as unestablished, not confirmed.
reverse: Static analyzer configs with path-sensitive checks enabled.

techniques.name: External contract verification
techniques.description: Checks claims about third-party behaviour (an API can return null, a library throws) against authoritative documentation, and grades how strong that proof is.

subtechniques.name: Documentation lookup
subtechniques.description: Fetch the exact library version's documentation or source.

subtechniques.name: Proof grading
subtechniques.description: Grade as definitive (spec or exhaustive enum), illustrative (an example) or unresolved.

craft: Resolve the dependency version from the lockfile.
Fetch that version's docs or source, not the latest.
Keep findings that rest on illustrative proof at lower severity.
reverse: Documentation MCP servers or doc lookup tools configured for the review agent.

techniques.name: Finding deduplication
techniques.description: Merges findings that describe the same problem from different reviewers, files or runs into one.

subtechniques.name: Semantic dedup
subtechniques.description: Cluster findings by embedding similarity and location.

subtechniques.name: Consolidation
subtechniques.description: Merge a cluster into one finding that keeps all evidence.

subtechniques.name: Fingerprinting across runs
subtechniques.description: Stable fingerprints so a finding is recognised on the next commit.

craft: Emit findings as SARIF or a common schema with file, line and rule.
Fingerprint by rule, file and normalised code, not line number.
Cluster the remainder by embedding and merge.
reverse: SARIF partialFingerprints, or a findings table keyed by fingerprint.

techniques.name: Severity scoring
techniques.description: Scores a finding from separate evidence axes (impact, persistence, detectability, reachability, scope, certainty) instead of a single guess.

subtechniques.name: Impact category
subtechniques.description: Data loss, security, crash, wrong behaviour, performance, leak or maintainability.

subtechniques.name: Persistence and detectability
subtechniques.description: Transient, until restart or permanent; loud, silent or delayed.

subtechniques.name: Blast radius
subtechniques.description: One operation, one user, a subset, broad or systemic.

subtechniques.name: Certainty basis
subtechniques.description: Demonstrated by a run, traced in code, inferred from a name, or assumed.

subtechniques.name: Standard vulnerability scoring
subtechniques.description: CVSS vectors, SSVC decisions and EPSS likelihood for security findings.

craft: Have the reviewer fill each axis separately with evidence.
Derive severity from the axes with a fixed table, never from free text.
Cap severity when certainty is inferred or assumed.
reverse: Severity rubrics in review guidelines, or CVSS vectors in security advisories.

techniques.name: Scope and relevance filtering
techniques.description: Keeps only findings that belong to this change: on changed lines, within the PR's intent, and fixable without reworking unchanged code.

subtechniques.name: Diff scoping
subtechniques.description: Report only on changed lines or their immediate context.

subtechniques.name: Intent scoping
subtechniques.description: Move findings outside the PR's intent to follow-up work.

subtechniques.name: Remediation scope
subtechniques.description: Check whether the fix stays inside the diff or reaches unchanged code.

craft: Filter by diff hunks first; it is cheap and removes most noise.
Check each remaining finding against the stated intent.
File out-of-scope findings as issues instead of review comments.
reverse: reviewdog -filter-mode settings, or bots that only comment on changed lines.

techniques.name: Noise budget
techniques.description: A fixed cap on how many findings are posted per change, filled in severity order, so the important ones are read.

subtechniques.name: Volume cap
subtechniques.description: At most N comments per review, highest severity first.

subtechniques.name: Carried findings
subtechniques.description: Findings that did not fit are kept and offered on the next run instead of dropped.

craft: Set the cap from how many comments reviewers actually address.
Sort by severity, then certainty.
Store the overflow and resurface it when the budget allows.
reverse: Review bot config with a maximum comment count.

techniques.name: Confidence calibration
techniques.description: Maps a reviewer's confidence to the observed rate of accepted findings and sets the posting threshold from that curve.

subtechniques.name: Calibration curve
subtechniques.description: Fit confidence against accepted or rejected outcomes.

subtechniques.name: Threshold per reviewer
subtechniques.description: Each reviewer gets its own threshold.

craft: Log confidence and the human outcome for every posted finding.
Fit a calibration model monthly.
Pick the threshold that meets a target precision.
reverse: Thumbs up or down reactions collected on bot comments.

techniques.name: Reflection pass
techniques.description: A self-critique step where the reviewer re-reads its own findings with fresh context and keeps, revises or withdraws each.

subtechniques.name: Finding reflection
subtechniques.description: Re-examine each finding against the code and the base-to-head diff.

subtechniques.name: Discussion-aware reflection
subtechniques.description: Include existing review threads so the reviewer does not repeat or contradict them.

craft: Run reflection with a different prompt and, ideally, a different model than the reviewer.
Pass the code, not the reviewer's reasoning.
Record why each withdrawn finding was withdrawn.
reverse: Multi-step review agent graphs with a critique node.

techniques.name: Past discussion check
techniques.description: Compares a finding with earlier review discussions: a repeat of something already decided is suppressed, a regression of a fixed issue is raised.

subtechniques.name: Repeat suppression
subtechniques.description: Do not re-raise what a human already dismissed.

subtechniques.name: Regression detection
subtechniques.description: Raise severity when a change reintroduces a previously fixed problem.

craft: Store resolved and dismissed threads with their code location and outcome.
Retrieve similar threads for each new finding.
Suppress repeats; escalate regressions.
reverse: Resolved review threads that mention an earlier PR or issue.

techniques.name: Ticket intent alignment
techniques.description: Checks a finding or a change against the linked ticket: behaviour the ticket declares intentional is not a bug, and requirements it lists must be present.

subtechniques.name: Intended per ticket
subtechniques.description: Suppress findings for behaviour the ticket explicitly asks for or defers.

subtechniques.name: Ticket coverage
subtechniques.description: List ticket requirements and check each against the diff.

craft: Link tickets in PR titles or branch names so they can be fetched.
Extract requirements as a structured list.
Match only on explicit statements; treat silence as unknown.
reverse: Ticket keys in branch names or PR titles, and issue-tracker integrations.

techniques.name: Plan and spec traceability
techniques.description: Checks each requirement in a plan or specification against the implementation: done in this change, done elsewhere, or not started, with gaps graded by severity.

subtechniques.name: Requirement tracing
subtechniques.description: Link requirement ids to code and tests.

subtechniques.name: Gap analysis
subtechniques.description: Report where the implementation departs from the plan's intent.

craft: Write specs with stable requirement ids.
Reference the ids in code comments or tests.
Report untraced requirements and code with no requirement.
reverse: specs/ or docs/adr directories, requirement ids in tests.

techniques.name: Functional spec verification
techniques.description: Runs the application and checks each functional requirement in a browser, returning met, partially met, not met or unverifiable with screenshot evidence.

subtechniques.name: Browser verification
subtechniques.description: An agent or script performs the flow and checks the outcome.

subtechniques.name: Evidence capture
subtechniques.description: Screenshot and annotate each verdict.

craft: Deploy a preview per PR.
Turn each acceptance criterion into a step and an observable outcome.
Attach screenshots to every verdict, including failures.
reverse: Preview deployment workflows and acceptance criteria in tickets.

techniques.name: Design conformance
techniques.description: Compares the rendered UI with the design it implements and reports layout, spacing, colour and copy differences.

subtechniques.name: Design-to-render comparison
subtechniques.description: Diff a screenshot against the exported design frame.

subtechniques.name: Annotated screenshots
subtechniques.description: Mark the differing regions so the fix is obvious.

craft: Export frames at the same viewport the test renders.
Compare with a tolerance and mask dynamic content.
Annotate differing regions on the screenshot.
reverse: Design links in tickets or PRs, and exported frames in the repository.

techniques.name: Review comment resolution
techniques.description: Checks whether a new commit actually addresses each open review comment before the thread is resolved.

subtechniques.name: Addressed check
subtechniques.description: Compare the comment's request with the code that changed after it.

subtechniques.name: Thread classification
subtechniques.description: Classify threads as addressed, disputed, deferred or open.

craft: Fetch open threads and the commits after each.
Ask whether the requested change is present, with the diff hunk as evidence.
Resolve only threads with evidence; reply on the rest.
reverse: Bots that resolve threads or post follow-ups after pushes.

techniques.name: Merge readiness
techniques.description: Combines checks, reviews, open threads and findings into one verdict on whether a change can merge.

subtechniques.name: Merge rules
subtechniques.description: Required checks, approvals and labels as code.

subtechniques.name: Merge verdict summary
subtechniques.description: A summary of what is still blocking, with links.

craft: Encode required checks and approvals in branch protection.
Add a bot that lists what is still blocking.
Merge automatically only when the verdict is clean.
reverse: Branch protection rules, .kodiak.toml or merge queue config.

techniques.name: Output guardrails
techniques.description: Validates what an automated reviewer or fixer produces before it is posted or committed: schema, policy and safety checks.

subtechniques.name: Schema validation
subtechniques.description: Reject malformed structured output and retry.

subtechniques.name: Policy rails
subtechniques.description: Block outputs that leak secrets, change protected files or exceed scope.

craft: Define the output schema and validate every response.
List protected paths and actions the bot may not take.
Log every blocked output for review.
reverse: Guardrail config files or validators around model calls.

techniques.name: Attack surface inventory
techniques.description: Lists every entry point and trust boundary: API endpoints, webhooks, queues, schedulers, parsers, CLIs, third-party scripts, model calls.

subtechniques.name: Network entry points
subtechniques.description: HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, raw socket and webhook receivers.

subtechniques.name: Asynchronous entry points
subtechniques.description: Queue consumers and scheduled jobs that act on external data.

subtechniques.name: Data parsers and deserialization
subtechniques.description: File, archive and object parsers that take untrusted input.

subtechniques.name: Infrastructure and configuration
subtechniques.description: Infrastructure as code, secrets management, caching and edge routing.

subtechniques.name: AI and model interactions
subtechniques.description: Prompts, tools and retrieved content that cross a trust boundary.

craft: Enumerate entry points from route tables, consumers and schedulers in code.
Describe the system as a model (pytm, Threagile) with data flows and trust boundaries.
Regenerate the model when entry points change.
reverse: threagile.yaml, pytm models or threat model documents in docs/.

techniques.name: Weakness discovery
techniques.description: For each entry point, searches for the weakness classes that apply to it: injection, broken access control, SSRF, deserialization, path traversal.

subtechniques.name: Per-surface weakness search
subtechniques.description: Apply the weakness classes relevant to each surface category.

subtechniques.name: Multi-tenancy isolation
subtechniques.description: Check every query and cache key for tenant scoping.

craft: Map each surface category to the weakness classes that apply.
Search with taint queries and an investigating agent.
Record each weakness with the entry point it is reachable from.
reverse: Security audit reports or issues labelled security.

techniques.name: Mitigation mapping
techniques.description: Checks whether each weakness is already mitigated by a control (validation, authorization middleware, rate limits) before reporting it.

subtechniques.name: Control inventory
subtechniques.description: List the security controls and where they apply.

subtechniques.name: Coverage check
subtechniques.description: Report entry points that bypass the controls.

craft: List controls as code locations (middleware, decorators, gateways).
Check each entry point passes through them.
Report only unmitigated weaknesses.
reverse: Auth middleware, rate limiter and validation layers in the code.

techniques.name: Exposure verification
techniques.description: Confirms which weaknesses are reachable from outside: external asset discovery and targeted checks against deployed endpoints.

subtechniques.name: External asset discovery
subtechniques.description: Enumerate domains, subdomains and exposed services.

subtechniques.name: Targeted confirmation
subtechniques.description: Send a request that demonstrates the weakness on a test deployment.

craft: Discover assets on a schedule.
Map findings to exposed assets.
Confirm with targeted templates against non-production environments.
reverse: Scheduled scan workflows and nuclei templates.

techniques.name: Risk prioritization
techniques.description: Orders confirmed weaknesses by exposure, exploit likelihood and impact so fixes start where risk is highest.

subtechniques.name: Decision trees
subtechniques.description: SSVC decisions from exploitation, exposure and impact.

subtechniques.name: Likelihood scores
subtechniques.description: EPSS for known vulnerabilities.

craft: Score exposure from the attack surface inventory.
Combine with likelihood and impact through a fixed decision tree.
Recompute when exposure changes.
reverse: Vulnerability management dashboards or SECURITY.md response targets.

techniques.name: Production error investigation
techniques.description: Investigates production errors from observability data, finds the responsible code and proposes a fix with a regression test.

subtechniques.name: Error-to-code mapping
subtechniques.description: Map a stack trace or log pattern to the commit and lines responsible.

subtechniques.name: Automated fix proposal
subtechniques.description: Open a change with the fix and a test that reproduces the error.

craft: Connect the agent to logs, traces and the repository read-only.
Require a reproduction before any fix.
Route fixes through the same review as human changes.
reverse: Observability integrations and incident runbooks in the repository.

techniques.name: Alert deduplication and triage
techniques.description: Groups related production alerts and errors and ranks them so investigation starts with the most impactful.

subtechniques.name: Alert correlation
subtechniques.description: Group alerts by fingerprint, service and time window.

subtechniques.name: Impact ranking
subtechniques.description: Rank by users affected, frequency and recency.

craft: Fingerprint errors by normalised stack trace.
Correlate within a time window per service.
Rank before routing to people or agents.
reverse: Alert routing and grouping rules in monitoring config.

techniques.name: Missed bug analysis
techniques.description: For each bug that escaped review, finds which technique should have caught it and why it did not, then clusters the causes.

subtechniques.name: Root cause trace
subtechniques.description: Replay the review trace for the PR that introduced the bug.

subtechniques.name: Cause clustering
subtechniques.description: Cluster root causes to find the systematic gaps.

subtechniques.name: Eval set growth
subtechniques.description: Add each missed bug to an evaluation set for the reviewers.

craft: Link every bug fix to the PR that introduced the bug.
Trace what each check and reviewer saw on that PR.
Add the case to the eval set and re-run reviewers on it.
reverse: Postmortems that name the introducing PR, and tracing for review agents.

techniques.name: Reviewer evaluation
techniques.description: Benchmarks reviewers on labelled changes: did they find the known bugs, and how many findings were wrong.

subtechniques.name: Labelled benchmark
subtechniques.description: PRs with known bugs and known clean changes.

subtechniques.name: Model as judge
subtechniques.description: A judge model matches reviewer findings to the labelled bugs.

subtechniques.name: Side-by-side comparison
subtechniques.description: Run two reviewer versions on the same set and compare.

craft: Build the set from real escaped bugs and from changes that needed no comments.
Score recall on bugs and precision on findings.
Gate reviewer changes on the benchmark.
reverse: eval/ or benchmarks/ directories with labelled cases.

techniques.name: Reviewer optimization
techniques.description: Tunes reviewer prompts and instructions against the evaluation set instead of by hand.

subtechniques.name: Prompt optimization
subtechniques.description: Search prompt variants against a metric.

subtechniques.name: Instruction updates from feedback
subtechniques.description: Update reviewer instructions from accepted and rejected findings.

craft: Define the metric first (from reviewer evaluation).
Optimize on a train split; report on a held-out split.
Review every prompt change like code.
reverse: Optimizer scripts and versioned prompt files in the repository.

techniques.name: Developer feedback capture
techniques.description: Records how developers respond to findings (fixed, dismissed, argued) and the sentiment of replies, as the ground truth for every other loop.

subtechniques.name: Outcome tracking
subtechniques.description: Was the finding fixed in a later commit, dismissed or ignored.

subtechniques.name: Reply sentiment
subtechniques.description: Classify replies as agreeing, disputing or neutral.

craft: Store every finding with its later outcome.
Sample disputed findings for human labelling.
Feed labels to calibration and evaluation.
reverse: Reactions and replies on bot comments, collected by a webhook.

techniques.name: CI failure analysis
techniques.description: Reads failing CI runs, separates real failures from flaky ones, and maps each to the job, step and change that caused it.

subtechniques.name: Flake detection
subtechniques.description: Re-run and compare to tell flaky tests from real failures.

subtechniques.name: Workflow structure analysis
subtechniques.description: Map jobs and steps to the checks they run (the scanner behind this site does this).

craft: Record test outcomes per run, not just the job status.
Quarantine tests that fail and pass on the same commit, and file an issue.
Never skip a test to get a green run.
reverse: Retry settings, flaky markers and test result uploads in CI.
